question.text: Under the presumptive taxation scheme (Section 44AD), what is the turnover limit for derivative traders?

answer.text: Rs. 2 crore (Rs. 3 crore if 95% of receipts are through digital/banking channels) — traders below this limit can declare 6% (digital) or 8% (cash) of turnover as income
Rs. 50 lakh — applicable only to professionals under Section 44ADA
Rs. 10 crore — the enhanced limit applies to all businesses including derivatives
No presumptive taxation is available for derivative traders

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 44AD allows presumptive taxation for businesses with turnover up to Rs. 2 crore (Rs. 3 crore where 95% of receipts are through digital/banking channels). Eligible traders can declare 6% (digital) or 8% (cash) of turnover as presumptive income. The Trap: Rs. 50 lakh is the limit for professionals under Section 44ADA, not the trader limit under 44AD. The 95%-digital condition is required for the Rs. 3 crore enhanced limit. Note: For derivative trading, turnover is computed as the total of favourable and unfavourable differences, premium received on sale of options, and the difference on reverse trades — premium paid is not added.
